prompt:
Before we order team shirts, we want to see how one size of the chart fits each person. Please add a command that runs as `python -m sizechart.fit CHART PEOPLE SIZE OUTPUT_FILE`. CHART and PEOPLE are a size chart and a people file in the same form that the sizechart command line reads. SIZE is the label of one size in the chart.

For each measure (chest, waist, hip) the fit is one of three named fit kinds: "tight" when the person's measurement in cm is above the maximum of the size, "loose" when it is below the minimum, and "regular" when it is inside the range (both ends included). The overall fit kind of a person is "tight" when any measure is tight, else "loose" when any measure is loose, else "regular". Measurements in inches are compared after conversion to cm.

The fit check for one person must also be usable on its own from other Python code: given one person and one size, it gives back one result that holds the person's name, the fit kind of each measure and the overall fit kind.

The command writes OUTPUT_FILE as CSV with the header row name,chest,waist,hip,fit and one row per person, in the order of the people file. The chest, waist and hip columns hold the fit kind of that measure, and the fit column holds the overall fit kind, each written as the word tight, regular or loose. A people file without rows gives a file with only the header row.

When SIZE is not a label in the chart, or when the chart or the people file cannot be read, the command tells the user what is wrong, exits with status 2 and does not write OUTPUT_FILE. In all other cases it exits with status 0.

Give every new public function a docstring that describes its parameters and return value. Add tests for the new feature.
